blocks.text: 1. Full Fine-Tuning
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446293339-846779086.png

Beam Search's own closing recap, already covered in Beam Search, pointed forward here. Full Fine-Tuning, updating every single weight of an already-pretrained model on new, task-specific data, is the most direct way to specialize a model.
This topic genuinely opens this course's own Fine-Tuning LLMs module, the foundation every other technique in this module builds on or departs from.
2. Recapping Pretraining
This connects back to pretraining, already covered generally in Transfer Learning. A pretrained model genuinely already knows broad, general language patterns from massive training data.
Fine-tuning genuinely takes that already-capable starting point and genuinely specializes it further, the exact relationship explored throughout the rest of this topic.
3. Updating Every Single Weight
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446293339-376768031.png
This connects back to recapping pretraining, already covered in this topic. Full fine-tuning genuinely continues training, but genuinely every single weight in the entire model stays trainable.
No genuinely parameter is genuinely frozen; the entire network genuinely keeps adjusting on new, task-specific data, the genuinely defining characteristic explored throughout the rest of this topic.

blocks.text: 4. Smaller Task Specific Dataset
This connects back to updating every single weight, already covered in this topic. The genuinely new training data is typically far smaller than the original pretraining corpus.
It is genuinely focused on one specific task, domain, or style rather than broad, general language, a genuinely important contrast explored throughout the rest of this topic.
5. Catastrophic Forgetting
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446293340-803924496.png
This connects back to a smaller, task-specific dataset, already covered in this topic. Genuinely updating every weight on a genuinely narrow dataset risks overwriting broad, general knowledge.
This genuinely real risk is called catastrophic forgetting, losing capabilities the model genuinely once had, a genuinely important failure mode explored throughout the rest of this topic.

blocks.title: info
blocks.content: This risk, already covered in this topic, directly explains why fine-tuning datasets, learning rates, and training duration are all genuinely chosen carefully, rather than simply training as long and as aggressively as possible.

blocks.text: 6. Compute And Memory Cost
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446293340-783399510.png
This connects back to catastrophic forgetting, already covered in this topic. Genuinely every trainable weight genuinely needs its own gradient and optimizer state stored during training.
For genuinely large models, this genuinely makes full fine-tuning extremely expensive in memory and compute, a genuinely real practical constraint explored throughout the rest of this topic.
7. One Full Copy Per Fine-Tuned Task

blocks.alt: One Full Copy Per Fine-Tuned Task
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446293340-90011724.png
This connects back to compute and memory cost, already covered in this topic. Genuinely every separate fine-tuned task genuinely produces its own entire, full-sized copy of the model.
Genuinely storing many separate fine-tuned versions genuinely multiplies that already-large storage cost, a genuinely real, compounding limitation explored throughout the rest of this topic.

blocks.title: info
blocks.content: This storage multiplication, already covered in this topic, directly motivates LoRA, covered as the next topic in this module, which genuinely avoids needing a full, separate model copy for every single fine-tuned task.

blocks.text: 8. Lower Learning Rates For Fine-Tuning
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446293540-33131700.png
This connects back to one full copy per fine-tuned task, already covered in this topic. Fine-tuning genuinely uses a genuinely much smaller learning rate than the original pretraining run.
This genuinely preserves most of the pretrained knowledge while still genuinely allowing careful adaptation, a genuinely important practical detail explored throughout the rest of this topic.

blocks.text: 11. Key Takeaways

items: Full fine-tuning updates every single weight of an already-pretrained model on new, task-specific data.
It builds directly on a pretrained model that already knows broad, general language patterns.
No parameter is frozen; the entire network keeps adjusting during fine-tuning.
The new training data is typically far smaller and more focused than the pretraining corpus.
Updating every weight on a narrow dataset risks catastrophic forgetting of general knowledge.
Every trainable weight needs its own gradient and optimizer state, making this expensive at scale.
Every separate fine-tuned task produces its own full-sized copy of the model, multiplying storage cost.
Fine-tuning uses a much smaller learning rate than pretraining, preserving most existing knowledge.
Next up: LoRA, a technique addressing the storage and compute cost of full fine-tuning.
